chapters.title: Hook
lines: Your laptop's on the TV. Or the projector. Or across the room, running the show.
You're over here. That's fine.
This is Edgepad five. A free, open-source Android app that turns your phone into the trackpad, keyboard, gamepad and remote for your laptop. Windows, Mac or Linux.

chapters.title: The surface
lines: The middle is a multi-touch trackpad. The corners are dials.
Slide for volume. Brightness. Zoom. Scrub through a video. Split the corners, and four dials become eight.
Change the volume on the laptop, and the dial moves with it.

chapters.title: Type and play
lines: Tap Controls, and the phone becomes whatever you need next.
A full keyboard, in six sizes, from a full board with a number pad down to a compact sixty percent.
A gamepad with two sticks and analog triggers. On Windows and Linux, your laptop sees a real Xbox controller, so your games just work.
Drag every control where your thumbs want it, or start from a racing, platformer or shooter layout.

chapters.title: Present and capture
lines: Giving a talk? Presenter steps through your slides, and a laser dot follows your thumb.
Capture a region, the full screen or a recording, and send it straight to your phone.

chapters.title: Move things
lines: Copy on one, paste on the other. Clipboard sync works both ways, and keeps a history.
Send files either way, up to two gigabytes each. Pick a few, watch them go, pause any time.
Macros open apps, folders and websites. Draw a shape on the trackpad, and one runs.

chapters.title: For developers
lines: Writing code? Turn on developer mode. Your Claude Code and Codex limits, your spend and every open session, right on your phone.
Pull requests and issues from GitHub, GitLab and more. Tap one, and it opens on the laptop.

chapters.title: Small things
lines: Air mouse: tilt to aim, hold a button to drag.
Falling asleep to a film? Edgepad puts the laptop to sleep when it ends.

chapters.title: Straight talk
lines: No account. No server. Your phone talks straight to your laptop, over Bluetooth, Wi-Fi or USB.
Windows is tested on real hardware. Mac and Linux are newer, so tell us on GitHub when something's off.

chapters.title: Next
lines: Coming in Edgepad six: screen mirroring, and remote access.

chapters.title: Get it
lines: Edgepad. Free and open source, on GitHub.
Your laptop, from anywhere in the room.
